    Create a model matrix with separated indicator column names

    model_matrix_sep.Rd

    stats::model.matrix() names indicator columns by pasting the column name and the factor level together (e.g., speciesGentoo). This function makes the same matrix but puts a separator between them (e.g., species_Gentoo).

    model_matrix_sep(data, ptype, sep = "_")

    Arguments

    data

    A data frame of predictors.

    ptype

    A zero-row data frame with the columns, types, and factor levels used to make the matrix (e.g., training_data[0, , drop = FALSE]). Using the same ptype for the training set and for new data guarantees the same columns. Character columns are not allowed since their levels are not retained; convert them to factors first.

    sep

    A single string placed between the column name and the level.

    Value

    A numeric matrix with the same number of rows as data.

    Details

    Indicators are made with treatment contrasts regardless of options("contrasts"). As with model.matrix(~ . + 0, data), the first factor (in ptype column order) gets an indicator for every level and later factors drop their first level. Ordered factors are treated as unordered factors. Logical columns are treated as factors with levels FALSE and TRUE. Missing values are retained as missing rows.

    Columns of data not in ptype are ignored. Values of a factor column that are not levels in ptype are converted to NA with a warning.

    Column names are found from the position of each column in the matrix, not by parsing names, so a column x with a level "x" becomes x_x.

    Examples

    if (rlang::is_installed("modeldata")) {
  penguins <- modeldata::penguins
  ptype <- penguins[0, c("species", "island", "bill_length_mm")]

  train_mat <- model_matrix_sep(penguins, ptype)
  head(train_mat)

  model_matrix_sep(penguins[1, ], ptype, sep = ".")
}
#>   species.Adelie species.Chinstrap species.Gentoo island.Dream island.Torgersen
#> 1              1                 0              0            0                1
#>   bill_length_mm
#> 1           39.1
